verdict.rationale: Supermemory documents a self-hosted mode, a single binary running on your own hardware with local embeddings and LLM, where "your data never leaves the building." That lets a user decide where data lives by running it themselves. Nothing shows region or residency selection on the hosted platform, so controlling location means taking on self-hosting. Missing for 10: region selection for the hosted service, documented data-residency guarantees (e.g. EU/US), and independent corroboration of the self-hosted data-locality claim.
